Upon reviewing the arguments, Peer 1's claim regarding *The Exorcist* remaining on a special prohibited-titles register under Article 140 is a hallucination. As correctly noted in the other assessments, the Netherlands dismantled its central film censorship board and outright movie bans decades ago (by 1980), transitioning entirely to an age-classification system (*Kijkwijzer*). 

The films commonly cited in historical censorship debates—such as *The Exorcist*, *A Clockwork Orange*, *The Texas Chain Saw Massacre*, and *Cannibal Holocaust*—are all legally available on home video, streaming platforms, and through theatrical distribution with standard adult age ratings. Because comprehensive, title-specific government bans on movies do not exist under current Dutch law, the correct option is that very few (if any) movies remain outlawed.

Final answer: G
